defectsFixedInThisWorkItem.description: Framework baseline integrity check failed OPEN. Implemented as inline shell ('if manifest exists, verify; else skip'), it reported SUCCESS while verifying nothing when 137 files were committed to the repository root instead of governance/framework/.
defectsFixedInThisWorkItem.impact: A green tick asserted the approved baseline was intact when the check had not examined a single file. False assurance is worse than no control.
defectsFixedInThisWorkItem.correction: Replaced with check_baseline_integrity.py distinguishing three states: ABSENT_EXPECTED (pass, genuine scaffold), ABSENT_UNEXPECTED (FAIL — framework content exists but not at the expected path), PRESENT (pass only if all hashes match).

defectsFixedInThisWorkItem.description: No check detected a flattened upload. 137 governance files landed at the repository root with all directory paths discarded; detection depended entirely on the owner requesting a manual file comparison.
defectsFixedInThisWorkItem.impact: Structural misplacement was invisible to every automated control.
defectsFixedInThisWorkItem.correction: New check_repository_layout.py refuses non-allowlisted files at the repository root and governance artifacts outside governance/. Reports 240 violations against the broken branch.
defectsFixedInThisWorkItem.foundBy: Owner asked for a file comparison against the repository rather than accepting the reported commit count.

defectsFixedInThisWorkItem.description: Assistant supplied the six required status-check names in a single code block; they were entered into the branch ruleset as ONE combined check name that can never report.
defectsFixedInThisWorkItem.impact: Merge blocked indefinitely on a permanently pending check. Incidentally prevented the bad merge, but by accident rather than design.
defectsFixedInThisWorkItem.correction: Ruleset rebuilt with seven separate check entries, each with source pinned to GitHub Actions.

toolingFinding.finding: Browser-based file upload failed three consecutive times in distinct ways: (1) silently skipped dot-prefixed paths, dropping the entire .github directory; (2) capped at 100 files per upload; (3) silently discarded directory structure, flattening 137 files to the root.
toolingFinding.significance: Each failure was invisible at the point of action and detectable only by post-hoc comparison. The tool provided no feedback that anything had been lost.
toolingFinding.resolution: Switched to GitHub Desktop, which shows full relative paths in its Changes view BEFORE committing. The same content committed correctly on the first attempt.
toolingFinding.lesson: The assistant should have changed tooling after the first failure rather than the third. Repeated adaptation to a tool that silently loses data is a false economy.
